messages.subject: Polygon with Telemetry
parts:
I am using the Royle and Young 2008 SCR model paired with Efford's 2011 MLE expansion to explore density estimates for the flat-tailed horned lizard using area search. I want to know how parameter estimates are affected by addition of variable amounts of telemetry data, so I am pairing the capture history and telemetry data, but have stalled with errors that I think must have to do with the mask or discretization of the polygon. 

I manually entered the polygon as:

YDMA2Manual <- make.poly (polylist = NULL, x = c(727600 ,727900,727900,727600 ), 
                          y = c(3592700, 3592700, 3593000, 3593000 ), exclusive
                          = FALSE, verify = TRUE)

YDMA21_<-read.csv("YDMA21DemoAdjust.csv")

CAPTHIST21<-make.capthist(YDMA21_, YDMA2Manual, fmt="XY")

YDMA21.fit<- secr.fit(CAPTHIST21)
YDMA21.fit

Tele11<-read.csv("Telemetry11.csv")
Tele11_ <- Tele11[, c("Session","Telemetry.ID","Occasion","Easting","Northing")]

Telemetry11 <- read.telemetry(data = Tele11_)
TeleCH21<- MS.capthist(CAPTHIST21,Telemetry11, type = c('independent'))

fit.ms <- secr.fit(TeleCH21, detectfn = 0 , trace = FALSE, verify = FALSE, mask = NULL) 

Once I've reached this point I get the error "Error in make.mask(tr, ...) : require spacing for rectangular mask" 

Do I need to discretize the polygon, how do I clarify the mask spacing/select a reasonable spacing (the plots are 300m x 300m)?
Thanks so much in advance for your help! 

Craig Fischer

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Polygon with Telemetry
parts:
Craig

Sorry for the delay. There are definitely some problems in 'secr' when addTelemetry() is applied to polygon data (strictly polygonX in the original study, I think), and the short-term solution is to discretize the capthist data:

CH <- discretize(CAPTHIST21)  # default 5-m pixels; fitting will be slow!
TeleCH <- addTelemetry(CH, Telemetry11, type = 'independent')
fit.ms <- secr.fit(TeleCH, detectfn = 'HHN' , trace = FALSE, verify = FALSE, mask = NULL)

However, I think this is a classic illustration of why one should not use telemetry data. Independent telemtry data contribute information only about sigma-hat, and even if sigma is known with certainty (and fixed in secr.fit) there is only a trivial change in the precision of D-hat. Fitting the capture + telemetry model failed for me with the data as they stand. I think the problem is that the telemetry data are centred elsewhere, outside the mask automatically generated by secr.fit(). Note also that the telemetry data (only 3 animals in the example you sent) require a very different sigma (as shown by RPSV) and are probably not applicable to the other dataset.

To fix the mask issue you can either construct a composite mask manually
telemmask <- make.mask(traps = do.call(rbind,telemetryxy(TeleCH)), spacing = 7.5, type = 'trapbuffer')
CHmask <- make.mask(traps=traps(TeleCH), spacing = 7.5, type = 'trapbuffer')
msk <- rbind(telemmask, CHmask)
or centre the telemetry data on the other survey area
centrexy <- function (xy) {
    mn <- apply(xy,2,mean) - apply(traps(CH),2,mean)
    xy <- sweep(xy, MAR=2, FUN='-', STATS = mn)
    xy
}
tmp <- telemetryxy(TeleCH)
telemetryxy(TeleCH) <- lapply(tmp, centrexy)

Murray
